clauses.reason: The only command is: "I hereby further exempt the said Claude L. Draper from compulsory retirement for age for a period of five years expiring June 22, 1956." The order sets its own five-year term. The exemption expired on June 22, 1956, recorded inclusive, with the exclusive reading (ends as June 22 begins) as the alternative. No held order revokes or extends it, so this is the first end. State on 2026-10-14: terminated.

inventory_overrides.reason: The machine inventory records this clause as the words 'for a period of five years expiring June 22, 1956' without the command. The operative command is the sentence that begins 'NOW, THEREFORE' and ends 'June 22, 1956.'; the four WHEREAS paragraphs are recitals, including the recital that his earlier term of office would expire June 22, 1951.

research_rationale:
EO 10255 (16 FR 5971; signed June 22, 1951; F.R. Doc. 51-7303) further exempts Claude L. Draper, a member of the Federal Power Commission, from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 "for a period of five years expiring June 22, 1956." The recitals say that Executive Order No. 9780 of September 19, 1946 had exempted him for an indefinite period not beyond the duration of his appointment or term of office, that his term would expire June 22, 1951, and that he had been appointed to a further five-year term. The operative command is the five-year exemption with a stated expiry. The first end is the own-terms date June 22, 1956, recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through that day), with the exclusive reading (ends as June 22 begins) as the alternative. The end is cited to the held Federal Register text of the order itself, a government printed copy (OCR text layer of the official PDF, whose page images were not opened).
